headline: Profit grows on FineMark scale despite integration costs
summary_short: Q2 net income rose 4.8% y/y to $159.8M ($1.10 diluted EPS) as double-digit net interest and fee-income growth outpaced a 21.5% jump in expenses tied to the FineMark acquisition; total deposits grew to $27.9B.
summary_long: Net income was $159.8M (+4.8% y/y; diluted EPS $1.10, +0.9% y/y, +14.6% q/q), as net interest income grew 12.5% to $315.1M and non-interest income grew 11.0% to $183.8M, driven mainly by trust and deposit fees. Non-interest expense rose 21.5% on FineMark integration — higher salaries, $12.0M litigation expense, and higher intangible amortization. Efficiency ratio widened to 58.40% from 54.77% y/y; net yield on earning assets improved to 3.77% from 3.70%. Total deposits grew to $27.9B (+$2.2B since year-end) largely from the FineMark acquisition. No numeric forward guidance was given. Total cash fell 24.3% q/q to $2,907.9M; shareholders' equity rose 1.3% q/q to $4,357.7M.

drivers.explanation: Net interest income rose 12.5% ($34.9M) on higher loan and securities income; non-interest income rose 11.0% on higher trust and deposit fees. Partly offset by non-interest expense up 21.5% from FineMark integration costs — higher salaries, $12.0M litigation expense, and higher intangible amortization.

Same income-statement dynamics as net income: net interest income +12.5% y/y and non-interest income +11.0% outpaced non-interest expense growth of 21.5% tied to FineMark integration and $12.0M of litigation costs.
EPS growth (+0.9% y/y) trailed net income growth (+4.8%) because weighted diluted shares outstanding grew 3.7% y/y (144.3M vs 139.2M), diluted by FineMark-related share issuance.
Same dynamic as diluted EPS: basic EPS growth of 0.9% y/y lagged net income's 4.8% increase due to a larger weighted average share count following FineMark-related share issuance.

Cash and equivalents fell 24.3% q/q as roughly $2.0 billion of financing outflows — deposit and repo declines plus $603.9M of FHLB borrowing repayments assumed in the FineMark deal — exceeded $866.7M of operating cash flow and $532.3M of investing inflows.
Equity rose modestly (+1.3% q/q) as net income and other comprehensive income gains were mostly offset by $111.3M of quarterly share buybacks and common dividends paid.

H1 2026 results were dominated by the Jan-1 FineMark acquisition (~$4.0B assets, $2.6B loans, $3.1B deposits, 13 FL/AZ/SC offices), which drove double-digit growth in net interest and fee income but also lifted non-interest expense 21.5% on integration, litigation, and amortization costs.
